title: BLR soundness over a prime field
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be normalized, meaning $f(0) = 0$. Fix $\varepsilon$ with $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear: every linear function $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ (one satisfying $g(x+y) = g(x)+g(y)$ for all $x,y$) has $\dist(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$, where $\dist(f,g) = \Pr_x[f(x) \ne g(x)]$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ obeys
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{p-1}{p}\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
the probability being taken over $x,y$ drawn independently and uniformly from $\bbz_p^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from every linear g: dist(f,g) ≥ ε
replaced:
If $p$ is prime and $f : \mathbb{Z}_p^n \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ is $\varepsilon$-far
from linear (normalized), then
\[
  \Pr[{\rm BLR\ accepts}\ f]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{p-1}{p}\bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon,
\]
recovering the prime-field soundness bound as a corollary of the general
result (using $\varphi(p)=p-1$).
